definitions.explanation: The turning of something into a liquid; in everyday use, almost always the way loose, water-soaked ground behaves like a liquid during an earthquake, so that buildings tilt and sand and water rise to the surface.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地面|じめん}→地面：00125_jimen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{液状化|えきじょうか}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{埋|う}め{立|た}て→埋め立て：12112_umetate⟧{地|ち}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{液状化|えきじょうか}しやすい。
examples.english: Reclaimed land is prone to liquefaction.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地震|じしん}→地震：01608_jishin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、{液状化|えきじょうか}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{傾|かたむ}き→傾く：00200_katamuku⟧、⟦{道路|どうろ}→道路：01481_douro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{泥水|どろみず}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{噴|ふ}き{出|だ}した→噴き出す：29265_fukidasu⟧。
examples.english: After the earthquake, liquefaction tilted houses and muddy water gushed onto the roads.

notes:
Used as a noun or as {液状化|えきじょうか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to liquefy). The full technical term is {液状化現象|えきじょうかげんしょう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {液状化現象|えきじょうかげんしょう}: the liquefaction phenomenon
- {液状化|えきじょうか}⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧: anti-liquefaction measures
- {液状化|えきじょうか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{被害|ひがい}→被害：02572_higai⟧: damage from liquefaction
- ⟦{地盤|じばん}→地盤：04035_jiban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{液状化|えきじょうか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: the ground liquefies
